assessment.where_you_stand: You are currently facing a difficult situation where your husband has left you and your two children without financial support for the last 6 months. As a woman and a mother, you are entitled to seek maintenance for yourself and your children, and you can approach the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) for free legal aid [KB:lsa_s12_legal_aid]. Legal provisions exist for the maintenance of wives and children [KB:src_bnss_2023_144_p2], but your case currently lacks formal documentation like your marriage certificate and details of your husband's income. Gathering these documents will strengthen your position significantly.

options.title: Contact DLSA for Free Legal Aid
options.what_to_do: Reach out to your local District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) or call the NALSA helpline at 15100 to get free legal advice and assistance from a lawyer.

options.title: Gather Documents and Evidence
options.what_to_do: Collect your marriage certificate, identity cards, text messages or any proof showing the duration of separation and lack of financial support.

proof_tips: Try to obtain a copy of your marriage certificate from the registrar or place of worship.
Keep records of any communication with your husband regarding household expenses or his absence.
Note down details of his employment, employer name, or bank accounts if you know them.
what_i_dont_know: Which state and city you are currently residing in
Whether your husband has a steady income or employment
If there are any prior agreements or domestic violence issues involved
assessment.needs_lawyer_reason: Family law matters involving maintenance, children, and divorce require formal legal representation to file petitions in court.
assessment.reply: It is very difficult to be left without support, especially with two children depending on you. Because you are seeking maintenance and a divorce, you should take immediate steps to secure legal guidance. As a woman and a mother, you are eligible for free legal assistance through the District Legal Services Authority under the Legal Services Authorities Act [KB:lsa_s12_legal_aid]. You can also contact the NALSA helpline at 15100 for immediate guidance [KB:lsa_s12_legal_aid]. Your first step should be to connect with your local DLSA office and gather any available identity or marriage documents. Do you currently have a copy of your marriage certificate or any written proof showing that your husband has stopped providing financial support?
